newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi ready for Italy budget talks with oppositioN.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi ready for Italy budget talks with oppositioN.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was quoted on Thursday as saying it was legitimate for the opposition to want to discuss the contents of Italy's 1998 budget if its passage through parliament is brought forward.

The centre-left government has proposed passing the budget by mid-August, four months early, in order to boost foreign confidence in Italy's ability to put its state finances in order for Europe's planned monetary union.
The weekly news magazine Panorama quoted Ciampi as saying that there had to be an agreement among parliamentary forces on the timing of the budget as a first step.
"But if the opposition asks to discuss the contents that is absolutely legitimate. It's part of the parliamentary game," Ciampi said in the interview, released by Panorama ahead of publication.

Silvio Berlusconi, leader of the centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance bloc, said on Tuesday that he was ready to consider bringing forward the budget as long as the package contained structural cuts on spending and health.
